project_metadata.job_description:
Here is a polished, professional job description tailored for Upwork. It is structured to attract high-quality, experienced mobile developers who understand the nuances of both platforms, localization workflows, and app size optimization.

Job Title
Senior Mobile Developer (Android & iOS) – Scoliometer App Update, 77+ Language Localization, & Size Optimization

Job Description
Overview
We are seeking an experienced, detail-oriented Mobile App Developer (or small agency) to update and optimize our existing application, Scoliometer App, for both Android and iOS platforms.

The core objectives of this project are to bring the current source code up to modern standards, implement an extensive localization strategy across dozens of languages, and optimize the app's footprint to ensure it remains as lightweight as possible.

Key Responsibilities
• OS & Framework Updates: * Update the existing source code to support the latest versions of iOS and Android OS/firmware.
• Refactor outdated APIs, deprecated libraries, and dependencies using current platform-recommended best practices (e.g., modern layout systems, Swift/Kotlin updates, or latest Flutter/React Native versions depending on the existing stack).

Massive Localization & Translation String Build:
• Set up and manage translation strings for global deployment.
• Google Play: Configure and implement localizations for 77 languages.
• App Store (iOS): Configure and implement localizations for 50 supported languages.
• Ensure proper RTL (Right-to-Left) layout support where applicable.

App Size Optimization:
• Audit and minimize the app binary size to keep it as small as possible.
• Implement Android App Bundles (.aab) and leverage iOS App Thinning/Slicing.

Optimize assets, graphics, and translation files to prevent bloat.
• Required Skills & Qualifications
• Proven experience in native (Swift/Kotlin) or cross-platform (Flutter/React Native) mobile development—please specify your expertise in your proposal based on our existing stack.
• Deep understanding of Apple App Store and Google Play Store localization guidelines and string management.
• Expertise in app size optimization techniques (asset compression, code stripping, dynamic delivery).
• Strong track record of updating legacy codebases to comply with the latest App Store and Google Play console requirements.
• Excellent communication skills and clean code documentation.

Application Questions for Candidates
• Can you share an example of a previous app you updated for modern OS compliance? What challenges did you face?
• What is our existing codebase stack (Native iOS/Android, Flutter, or React Native)? [Note: We will provide access to the repository to the shortlisted candidates].
• What strategies do you typically use to keep the app binary size as small as possible when dealing with over 50+ localized language files?

Project Type & Budget
• Project Type: Deliverable-based / Fixed-price (or Hourly for the right candidate)

Experience Level: Expert / Senior

messages.text:
I carefully reviewed the source code for both Android and iOS. Below is what I identified and the improvements I would make.

**Present Condition**

The apps are functional, but both require fixes before they can be submitted to the stores today.

**Problems on iOS**

* The app relies on UIWebView, which Apple has removed, so Apple will reject it when submitted.
* It does not include the Privacy Manifest file required by Apple since May 2024.
* The localization setup does not work. Although there are 20 language folders, their translation files are absent, meaning the app always displays English regardless of the phone's selected language.
* Its signing certificates expired in 2015.
* Info.plist and the main ViewController.m are not present in the source you provided. I will need both files to work on iOS.

**Problems on Android**

* At 89 MB, the app is unnecessarily large. It does not use an Android App Bundle, code shrinking, or image optimization.
* It asks for the sensitive READ\_PHONE\_STATE permission without using it, which may cause Google Play review problems in certain regions.
* One removed sensor API is still in use, along with several other deprecated calls.
* Because of an HTTP/HTTPS compatibility problem, the Chinese video on Youku fails on modern Android.
* The libraries are extremely outdated and are 7+ versions behind the current releases.

**Improvements I Would Make**

1. Restore store-readiness:
* Replace UIWebView on iOS.
* Include the mandatory Privacy Manifest.
* Renew the certificates.
* Delete the unused dangerous Android permission.

2. Substantially decrease the app size:
* Move Android to the App Bundle format.
* Turn on code shrinking.
* Delete duplicate and unused images.
* On iOS alone, I identified approximately 10 MB of duplicated files.

3. Correct the localization implementation:
* Reconstruct the nonfunctional iOS translation system.
* Align the Android language files, since some languages are missing 26 strings.
* Rework the tutorial images so adding languages no longer requires new graphic design changes each time.

4. Modernize the old code:
* Update the dependencies.
* Substitute deprecated APIs.
* Bring the YouTube player implementation up to date.

5. Implement RTL support if required:
* Arabic, Hebrew, and Persian currently do not display correctly.

6. Meet current platform standards:
* Android 35, which Google will require soon.
* iOS 15+.

**Information Needed for Exact Timelines**

1. The iOS project seems incomplete because Info.plist and ViewController.m are missing. Can you provide the complete project?
2. Is the keystore password for the Android signing key available? The supplied files did not contain it.
3. Should the Chinese video on Youku remain, or may it be removed?
4. When adding languages, do you want the entire app localized or just translated store listing pages?

Once you confirm these points, I can prepare a detailed plan and estimated timeline.

1) Bend: Ask the person to bend forward from the waist, letting their arms hang down with their palms together.

2) Align: Position the phone horizontally over their upper back, with the spine centered in the middle notch.

3) Measure: Slowly move the phone up along the spine. It will tilt sideways according to the curve—the highest number shown is your degree.
